slides.title: Physical Changes 🧊
slides.text: In a physical change, no new substance is formed! The shape, size, or state may change, but it is still the same material. Most physical changes are easily reversible — like melting ice or dissolving salt in water.
slides.spoken: In a physical change, no new substance is formed! The shape or state may change, but it is still the same material. They are usually reversible, like melting ice or dissolving salt.

slides.title: Chemical Changes 🔥
slides.text: In a chemical change, one or more brand-new substances are formed! They have completely different properties and the change is usually irreversible — like burning paper, cooking food, or rusting iron.
slides.spoken: In a chemical change, a brand new substance is formed! They are usually irreversible, like burning wood, cooking food, or rusting iron.

slides.title: Composition of Air 🌬️
slides.text: Air is a mixture of gases! Nitrogen is the most abundant gas, making up about 78% (four-fifths) of air. Oxygen is about 21% and is needed for breathing and burning. Carbon dioxide and other gases make up the rest.
slides.spoken: Air is a mixture of gases! Nitrogen makes up about seventy-eight percent of air, while oxygen makes up about twenty-one percent.

slides.title: Land and Sea Breezes 🌊
slides.text: During the day, land heats faster than water; warm air rises and cool air from the sea flows in — this is the Sea Breeze! At night, land cools faster than water, and the breeze blows from land to sea — the Land Breeze!
slides.spoken: During the day, land heats faster than water and cool sea air blows inward as a sea breeze. At night, land cools faster and a land breeze blows outward.

slides.title: Ventilators & Exhaust Fans 🏠
slides.text: Warm air is lighter than cool air, so warm stale air rises to the top of a room. Ventilators placed high near the ceiling let this warm air escape! Exhaust fans force out smoke, heat, and odors from kitchens and bathrooms.
slides.spoken: Warm air rises because it is lighter. Ventilators near the ceiling let warm stale air escape, while exhaust fans quickly remove smoke and odors.

challenges.question: Which of the following is a PHYSICAL change?
challenges.hint: Think: in which change is no new substance formed and it can be easily reversed?
challenges.misconception: Melting ice is physical because water remains the same substance and can be frozen back into ice. Burning and rusting form brand-new substances!

challenges.question: Drag each change to Physical or Chemical change!
challenges.hint: Physical changes do not form new substances (like melting ice). Chemical changes create new materials (like burning wood).
challenges.misconception: Remember: dissolving, boiling, and melting are physical changes. Burning, rusting, and cooking are chemical changes because new substances are formed!

challenges.question: Which gas is the MOST abundant (largest part) in the air?

challenges.misconception: Many think air is mostly oxygen because we breathe it, but Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air, while Oxygen is only 21%!

challenges.question: What is the main purpose of an exhaust fan in a kitchen?
challenges.answer: To remove warm stale air, smoke, and odors

To bring in hot air from outside
To light up the cooking stove
